title: House Bill 932: Advisory Question on the Official State Gun

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the Idaho Legislature through House Bill 932 (2026), which passed the House 68-0-2 and the Senate 32-0-3. The question is non-binding.

question.text: Which of the following guns should be designated as the state gun of Idaho? Please choose only one answer. Winchester Model 1894 (.30-30); Winchester Model 1873 “Gun that Won the West” (.44-40); 1873 Colt Single Action Army Revolver “Peacemaker” (.45 Colt); M1 Garand rifle (.30-06); Colt M1911 .45 automatic Colt pistol (.45 ACP); or Remington Model 700 bolt-action rifle (.30-06)

summary.text: The official Brief Statement of Purpose says: “This advisory question asks Idahoans to designate which gun they would like to have as the official Idaho State Gun. This is a non-binding measure, and the Legislature would have to take action during a future legislative session to officially designate a gun as the Idaho State Gun.” The pamphlet gives a brief description of each of the six firearms. No fiscal impact is stated in the retrieved pamphlet text.

measure.yesMeans: Voters choose one of the six listed firearms as their preference for the official Idaho state gun; the result is advisory and does not itself designate a state gun.
measure.noMeans: This is a multiple-choice advisory question, not a yes/no measure; voters who do not mark an answer express no preference, and the Legislature would have to act in a future session to designate a state gun.

researchNotes: Ballot list confirmed against the Secretary of State's VoteIdaho.gov General Election page, which lists exactly four statewide items (HJR 4, HJR 6, Proposition One, and the State Gun advisory question). This is a six-way advisory question, so yesMeans/noMeans are adapted from the official purpose statement. The pamphlet publishes no arguments for or against this question, so none are included.
